title: The Shell That Bounced Back
set_language: ONE persistent Manchester 1909 dark scattering lab (gold foil, scintillation screen, microscope); then empty football stadium pea metaphor; then 1910s study desk for the charge-guess beat. Say 'same 1909 dark scattering set' / 'same empty stadium set' / 'same study desk'. Never 'same DNA'. Never name Rutherford/Geiger/Marsden/Thomson/van den Broek in Flow prompts.
continuity_lock: Picture change every 4–6 s. Explorer once only on stadium pea. Readable finished faces when people appear — describe, do not name. Real element symbols only if any (prefer blank boards).
explorer_lock: Exactly ONE Explorer plate: 16_explorer_stadium_pea. Film-wide Explorer budget: 1 used (Part 02); this plate = 2 of 3. On model — round gold glasses, teal coat, finished hair. Attach Explorer reference.
forbidden: HARD REJECT: Orbit; photoreal; Ken Burns; gore; lava drip; DNA helix; naming Rutherford/Geiger/Marsden/Thomson/van den Broek in the prompt; garbled dials; SEE labels; Explorer except plate 16; war gore.
motion_lock: Real Veo motion every plate. No freeze-pad.
quality_note: Veo 3.1 Quality for green scintillation / alpha glow / nucleus glow / charge-link glow. Fast otherwise.
credit_fallback: If Flow credits would drop below ~150 buffer, mint remaining plates with the SAME Veo 3.1 model via Gemini API (Quality→veo-3.1-generate-preview, Fast→veo-3.1-lite-generate-preview). Log path+spend per plate. Never mix other models.
board_split_2026_09_27: Split prior 10-plate board into 22 plates ≤~6 s for picture-change rule.

plates.vo_land: Manchester, nineteen-oh-nine. Ernest Rutherford has a new kind of bullet.
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. Manchester 1909 dark scattering lab. Bearded physicist with a big moustache stands at a gold-foil apparatus on a wooden bench — readable finished face. Continuous soft approach. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit. No readable fake text.
plates.prompt_try2: Same 1909 lab. Wider: apparatus fills frame, physicist soft in background. Continuous soft push. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Alpha particles, tiny and fast, thrown out by radioactive rocks.
plates.prompt: Same 1909 scattering set. Tiny glowing alpha bullets stream from rough radioactive rock samples toward the apparatus. Continuous stream. Quality clean glow — no lava drip. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit.
plates.prompt_try2: Same set. ECU: glowing particle trails leave the rock samples. Continuous trails. Quality. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: His assistant Hans Geiger and a young student called Ernest Marsden fire them at gold beaten thinner than paper.
plates.prompt: Same 1909 dark lab. A moustached assistant and a young student fire glowing particles at a paper-thin gold foil in a frame. Continuous fire. Silent. Readable finished faces. No Explorer. No Orbit. No text signs.
plates.prompt_try2: Same lab. Side view: foil frame centre, two figures at the source. Continuous soft push. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: …gold beaten thinner than paper. Picture yourself in that room.
plates.prompt: Same 1909 set. ECU of paper-thin gold foil held in a brass frame — light catches the leaf. Continuous gentle shimmer. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit.
plates.prompt_try2: Same set. Hands adjust the foil frame; leaf flutters once. Continuous. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Picture yourself in that room. The lights are off,
plates.prompt: Same 1909 scattering room. Gas lamps extinguish — the lab falls into deep darkness with only faint apparatus glints. Continuous darken. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit.
plates.prompt_try2: Same room. Wider dark: benches and foil frame as silhouettes. Continuous fade-to-dark. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: and you sit in the dark until your eyes adjust. You look through a microscope at a small screen.
plates.prompt: Same dark 1909 room. POV settles toward a microscope eyepiece aimed at a small scintillation screen. Continuous lean-in. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit.
plates.prompt_try2: Same dark room. ECU eyepiece rim; screen soft beyond. Continuous soft push into the eyepiece. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Each time a particle hits it, you see a tiny green flash, and you count it.
plates.prompt: Same dark room through the eyepiece. Tiny clean green scintillation flashes appear one by one on the small screen — count them. Continuous flashes. Quality green glow. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit. No lava.
plates.prompt_try2: Same eyepiece POV. Closer on the screen: sparse green pin-flashes. Continuous count rhythm. Quality. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Now, if Thomson's pudding is right, every bullet should punch straight through.
plates.prompt: Same set. Diagram-feel cutaway: glowing bullets punch straight through a soft pudding-like atom model into the foil. Continuous punch-through. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit. No named labels.
plates.prompt_try2: Same idea. Wider: stream of bullets races through a soft sphere toward open space. Continuous race. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Almost all of them do.
plates.prompt: Same 1909 foil set. A dense stream of glowing bullets passes straight through the gold foil — almost every one. Continuous stream. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit.
plates.prompt_try2: Same foil. Side tracking shot following bullets that keep going. Continuous follow. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: But about one in eight thousand bounces back.
plates.prompt: Same foil set. Almost all bullets pass; ONE glowing bullet ricochets steeply back toward camera — surprise. Continuous bounce. Quality glow. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit.
plates.prompt_try2: Same foil. ECU: single bullet hits and reverses hard. Continuous reverse. Quality. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Rutherford said it was as if you fired a huge shell at a piece of tissue paper,
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. Wonder metaphor (not war gore): a huge artillery shell races toward a sheet of tissue paper. Continuous approach. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit. No blood.
plates.prompt_try2: Same metaphor. Wider: tissue paper fills frame; shell enters from depth. Continuous approach. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: and it came back and hit you.
plates.prompt: Same metaphor set. The huge shell bounces off the tissue and flies back toward camera — impossible surprise, wonder not gore. Continuous rebound. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit.
plates.prompt_try2: Same metaphor. Side view: shell arcs back after the tissue kiss. Continuous arc. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Then, in nineteen-eleven, he explains it. Nearly all of an atom's mass is packed into a tiny, positive centre,
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. Cutaway atom: nearly all mass gathers into a tiny bright positive centre. Continuous pack-in. Quality soft glow. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit. No DNA helix.
plates.prompt_try2: Same cutaway. Camera pushes toward the tiny centre as mass concentrates. Continuous push. Quality. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: which he calls the nucleus. The electrons sit far outside it.
plates.prompt: Same atom cutaway. Tiny glowing nucleus at centre; a few electrons sit far out on distant orbits. Continuous orbit drift. Quality. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit robot. No DNA.
plates.prompt_try2: Same cutaway. Wider empty middle; electrons tiny on the far rim. Continuous slow orbit. Quality. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Everything in between is almost empty. How empty?
plates.prompt: Same atom cutaway. Vast empty space between the tiny centre and distant electrons — almost nothing. Continuous soft pull-back revealing emptiness. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit. No DNA.
plates.prompt_try2: Same cutaway. Extreme wide: centre is a pinprick in black void. Continuous pull-back. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Imagine you are standing in the middle of a football stadium holding a pea. If the atom were the whole stadium, the nucleus would be that pea.
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. Giant empty football stadium at dusk. Exactly ONE Explorer on the centre spot holds up a tiny pea, looking up at the far stands. Continuous look-up. Attach Explorer reference. Silent. No Orbit. No twins.
plates.prompt_try2: Same empty stadium. Wider: Explorer tiny in the middle holding the pea aloft. Continuous soft orbit around him. Silent. Exactly ONE Explorer.

plates.vo_land: The electrons would be somewhere out past the back row of seats.
plates.prompt: Same empty stadium set. Camera lifts past empty back-row seats toward the far rim — electrons would live out there. Continuous lift. Silent. No Explorer required. No Orbit. No crowd fill.
plates.prompt_try2: Same stadium. Tracking along empty seats toward the outer bowl. Continuous track. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Everything else, all around you, is nothing at all.
plates.prompt: Same empty stadium set. Vast empty pitch and stands — nothing at all around the centre spot. Continuous slow spin revealing emptiness. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit. No crowd.
plates.prompt_try2: Same stadium. Extreme wide empty bowl under dusk sky. Continuous soft drift. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: That raised a new question. If every element has its own nucleus, what makes one nucleus different from another?
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. Two tiny glowing nuclei side by side — same size, different soft charge colour — question mood. Continuous soft compare drift. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit. No text signs.
plates.prompt_try2: Same idea. Wider: several nuclei floating; camera picks two. Continuous drift. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: A Dutch lawyer and amateur scientist, Antonius van den Broek, had a bold guess:
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. 1910s study desk. A Dutch lawyer-amateur scientist (readable finished face, period suit, no powdered wig) studies a blank periodic-table board beside a glowing nucleus sketch. Continuous lean-in. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit. No garbled letters — blank board only.
plates.prompt_try2: Same study. ECU: hands hover over blank table board and nucleus sketch. Continuous hover. Silent. No Explorer. No fake text.

plates.vo_land: An element's place in the table might equal the positive charge in its nucleus.
plates.prompt: Same study desk idea. A blank table place marker links by a soft glow-line to a tiny positive charge inside a nucleus — guess, not proof. Continuous glow connect. Quality. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit. No fake element letters.
plates.prompt_try2: Same idea. Closer on the glowing positive centre tied to a blank place slot. Continuous pulse. Quality. Silent. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: It was a brilliant guess, but nobody could measure it. Yet.
plates.prompt: Same study set. The glow-link dims; measuring instruments sit unused on the desk — the guess hangs unanswered. Continuous soft settle-with-motion. Silent. No Explorer. No Orbit. No Ken Burns-only still.
plates.prompt_try2: Same desk. Wider: unanswered glow fades while camera drifts. Continuous drift. Silent. No Explorer.
